description:
Second published-cutover fixture: `reviewPolicy: scope` (not mixed into the ticket-policy epic test).

## Background

Scope policy closes tickets from evidence then independently reviews the aggregate before declaring the epic complete. Dependents may start before aggregate review finds a problem. That tradeoff must be proven, not only described in prompts. Do not collapse this into the ticket-policy fixture.

## Scenario

1. Epic with two tickets, policy scope.
2. `/bw run`, implement both, parent accepts/closes from evidence **without** per-ticket review children.
3. Dependent may start after close (not after settle).
4. One immutable scope review child (`taskType: reviewScope`) against the aggregate.
5. Blocking finding → in-scope fix or reopen path as prompt policy; re-review/revalidate as scripted parent turns.
6. Epic close only after scope review dispositions are done.
7. Logs: policy=scope, ticket ids, whether a ticket-review child was (must not be) launched, scope-review child id, dispositions.

## Success criteria

- No per-ticket `reviewImplementation` children under scope policy.
- Ticket-policy fixture still requires them (other issue).
- tmux absent. Scripted parent, no paid LLM.

## Test plan

- Dedicated e2e script with step logging (timestamp, action, issue id, child id, policy).
- Failure dumps last packet and `bw show` of the epic.

## Considerations

Same blockers as the ticket-policy epic e2e. Runs after that fixture so the harness exists; do not copy-paste two harnesses—share the scripted-parent helper.
title: Prove scope-policy epic fixture without per-ticket review children
